name: Relevance
description: Measures how well the summary captures the key points of the original news article, ensuring that all important information is included.
scale: Scale from 1 to 5, where 1 means the summary misses most key points, and 5 means it includes all key points.

name: Conciseness
description: Evaluates whether the summary is succinct and free of superfluous details, maintaining brevity while still informative.
scale: Scale from 1 to 5, where 1 means the summary is overly verbose or includes unnecessary details, and 5 means it is concise and to the point.

name: Clarity
description: Assesses how clear and understandable the summary is, with well-structured sentences and logical flow.
scale: Scale from 1 to 5, where 1 means the summary is confusing or poorly structured, and 5 means it is exceptionally clear and well-organized.

name: Accuracy
description: Determines the factual correctness of the information presented in the summary, ensuring there are no inaccuracies compared to the original article.
scale: Scale from 1 to 5, where 1 means the summary contains several inaccuracies, and 5 means it is completely accurate and factual.

name: Language Quality
description: Evaluates the grammatical correctness, style, and readability of the summary, focusing on proper language use.
scale: Scale from 1 to 5, where 1 means the summary contains numerous grammatical errors or awkward phrasing, and 5 means it is grammatically flawless and well-written.
